Soaring costs: Crew members preparing the Villa Vie Odyssey cruise ship for departure from the Sihanoukville Autonomous Port in Preah Sihanouk province. 
— Reuters 
 After disembarking more than 200 passengers who had paid tens of thousands of dollars to live on board for years, the Villa Vie Odyssey cruise ship departed from the country.
 Last week, the vessel’s owner, Florida-based Villa Vie Residences, suspended operations and forced passengers off the ship at the port town of Sihanoukville, saying ‌fuel price increases from the Iran conflict had made operations prohibitively expensive.
 The ship left yesterday with no passengers and around 50 crew, according to Taing Sochitkrishna, head of the Sihanoukville ­tourism department.
 He said around 100 passengers remained in Cambodia, while the others flew to other destinations in the region.
 Passengers unloaded their last belongings from the vessel on Tuesday, and many said they did not expect to return to the ship.
 “There are still many things on the ship that I wish I could take with me,” said Shirine Thomas, of Wilmington, North Carolina, shortly after collecting some final items.
 The Villa Vie Odyssey had been cruising the world for at least 755 days as one of only a handful of ships that offered passengers the opportunity to rent or buy long-term or even permanent ​residences on board.
 Sixty-seven-year-old retired high school teacher Mary Ann Demsar from Ontario, Canada, said the owners had provided no information on whether the voyage would continue.
 “We don’t get any clear indication from the owners of Villa Vie as to what is happening,” she said. “The only information we get is from the wonderful government and the representatives here.” — Reuters
